subject: JazzyAdmin browser-based SaaS store administration dashboard and sign-in experience
scope: Redesign the existing login screen and authenticated dashboard shell across all current hash-routed screens, preserving existing functionality and sample-data behavior.
primaryGoal: Make store administration feel modern, responsive, visually refined, and easier to scan and operate across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
audience: Small online-store administrators managing products, orders, customers, analytics, reports, messages, support, and account preferences.
offer: A browser-only store admin workspace with dashboards, analytics, reporting, product and customer management, order workflows, messaging, support, and settings.
primaryAction: Sign in, then monitor store performance and take operational actions such as reviewing orders, managing products, responding to messages, exporting reports, and updating settings.
creativeControl: High within the existing product and functional constraints. Refresh the art direction, hierarchy, density, surfaces, responsive composition, and motion system toward a distinctive 2026 product interface, using tasteskill.dev only as a directional reference for polished transitions and interaction quality. Keep JazzyAdmin recognizable and avoid generic AI-generated dashboard styling.
requiredContent: Authenticated application shell: Fixed or adaptive sidebar with Main, Management, Communication, and Support navigation groups; responsive mobile drawer; top header with menu, breadcrumb, global search, theme toggle, notifications, and user menu.

Dashboard: Time-based greeting, store overview totals, revenue and order metrics, sales overview chart, revenue analytics chart, recent orders, top products, activity timeline, calendar, tasks, notes, and weather widget.
Analytics: Revenue, orders, customers, and conversion summary metrics; revenue trend, category sales, category distribution, customer growth, revenue table, and CSV export.

Reports: Daily, weekly, monthly, and custom-range controls; period summary, chart, report-type cards for sales, revenue, customer, inventory, tax, and performance; PDF and Excel-style browser exports.
Customers: Search and status filters; customer table with avatar, contact details, status, order count, spend, and join date; pagination; add, view, edit, and confirm-before-delete actions.

Products: Search, category and stock filters, sorting, grid/table switcher, product cards or rows with image, SKU, pricing, discount, stock, and status; selection, bulk delete, pagination, and navigation to Add Product.

Add Product: Product form for name, description, category, SKU, price, discount, stock, tags, and image upload; drag-and-drop previews; discounted-price preview; save draft and publish validation flows.
Orders: Search and status filters; order table with customer, item count, total, status, and date; order detail modal; print invoice, download invoice, and export actions.
Messages: Conversation list with avatars, previews, timestamps, unread states, thread view, compose field, and browser-only replies for the supplied sample conversations.
FAQ and Help Center: Six FAQ accordion topics; help search, support categories, popular articles, contact form, and supplied support details.
Settings: Profile, security, email preferences, notification preferences, appearance controls including dark mode, compact sidebar, and animations, plus language and timezone settings.

Sign-in experience: Sign In, Register, and Forgot Password tabs; validation, password visibility, strength feedback, remember-me option, theme toggle, and visible Google/GitHub interface buttons without real social authentication.
constraints: Preserve the existing browser-only architecture using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript modules with no live server or backend assumptions.
Preserve hash-based navigation, localStorage persistence for user, theme, sidebar, drafts, and preferences, and existing sample data behavior.
Keep all existing operational behaviors including validation, confirmations, toasts, modals, charts, filters, pagination, exports, print views, and responsive sidebar drawer behavior.
Maintain light and dark themes, accessible labels and focus states, readable contrast, keyboard-friendly controls, and reduced-motion support.
Use responsive layouts for desktop, tablet, and narrow mobile screens; avoid relying on hover-only interactions.
Use motion purposefully for page transitions, navigation, filters, tabs, drawers, modals, charts, loading states, and feedback without making the dashboard feel distracting.
Do not introduce unsupported business claims, live integrations, real authentication, or fabricated product outcomes.
External Font Awesome, Chart.js, Google Fonts, and image URLs are currently referenced by the project and should remain replaceable if offline behavior becomes a requirement.
brandInputs: Product name: JazzyAdmin, from FUNCTIONS-AND-UX.md and the current sidebar/login markup.

Current visual palette: indigo primary #4F46E5 light / #6366F1 dark, violet secondary #7C3AED light / #8B5CF6 dark, plus green, amber, red, and blue semantic colors, from FUNCTIONS-AND-UX.md and css/variables.css.
Current typography: Inter with Poppins and system UI fallbacks, from FUNCTIONS-AND-UX.md and css/base.css.

Current visual language: light and dark themes, gradient brand mark, soft bordered cards, rounded corners, subtle shadows, Font Awesome icons, and Chart.js visualizations, from FUNCTIONS-AND-UX.md and css/*.css.
Current structure: fixed sidebar, top header, scrolling content region, responsive drawer, and short fade/rise route transition, from FUNCTIONS-AND-UX.md and js/layout.js/js/router.js.
Existing logo treatment: letter J in a gradient rounded-square mark, from index.html, login.html, and js/layout.js.
assumptions: The request is for a redesign of the existing admin product interface, not a marketing website, so dashboard rules apply and no marketing landing-page section minimum is needed.

The existing project files are the source of truth for current functionality and brand tokens; no new brand identity, logo, business claims, or backend capabilities are being introduced in this brief.
The redesign should cover both the authenticated dashboard and login experience because the supplied project specification defines both as part of the product.

Animation should be richer than the current 0.25s fade/rise system, but remain purposeful, performant, accessible, and suppressible through the existing appearance setting and reduced-motion preferences.
The referenced tasteskill.dev URL is treated as a visual direction only. The brief does not require copying its layout, assets, or content.
The current sample data, support details, and demo credentials remain demonstration content and should not be presented as production claims.
